chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Ibrahim عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who is traveling, then arrives and enters the houses of Makkah: should he perform the salat in full, or should he remain shortening it until he enters upon his family? He said: Rather, he should remain shortening it until he enters upon his family.

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: his family or household, whose entry marks the end point mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.بُيُوتَ مَكَّةَ: the houses of Makkah that the traveler enters upon returning
key_terms.مُسَافِرًا: a person in a state of travel
key_terms.مُقَصِّرًا: shortening the salat as a traveler
key_terms.يُتِمُّ ٱلصَّلَاةَ: performs the salat in its complete form

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler stop shortening the salat after returning from السفر?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the traveler returning from a journey. It states that merely entering the houses of Makkah does not end the traveler's concession; he continues to shorten the salat until he enters upon his family.
